title: Payments initiation conceptual model
meaning: Payment connects obligation, processing, identification, status, execution, tax, currency exchange and settlement account. Initiation specializes execution; credit-transfer and direct-debit mandates specialize Mandate; Garnishment specializes PaymentObligation. The long lower association connects Payment and CashAccount. Relationship-end labels are retained together without inferring message sender/receiver roles.

title: Payments clearing and settlement conceptual model
meaning: Payment processing connects execution, service level, bank-transaction classification, mandate and contact point. Payment connects account, payment-party role, identification, timing request and status. Cash settlement connects instruction and cash account. Role and system specializations, organisation self-association and every unlabelled source line are retained. The source places “+ ClearingSystemMemberIdentificationType” above the organisation-identification/member region, away from its connector. The label is assigned to the existing OrganisationIdentification–CashClearingSystemMember line using the same workbook FullBusinessModel!A2990:F2990 and inverse A635:F635, which explicitly identify both endpoints and this association-end name. This is a documented resolution of layout ambiguity, not an added relationship; see issue-000025. No CashClearingSystemMember–CashClearingSystem association is drawn in the supplied figure.

title: Operational cash-management role players
meaning: Role associates with its RolePlayer. Information, payment and system-party roles specialize Role, while Party and System specialize RolePlayer. System roles and clearing-member identification remain distinct from the party or institution playing them. TransactionAdministrator specializes SystemPartyRole and associates with CashClearingSystem.

title: Operational cash-management payment-related components
meaning: Payment instruction has both a generalization to PaymentExecution and a separate Previous/Next association. Payment relates to its obligation, status, cash account and credit method. BookEntry specializes CreditInstrument and connects CashEntry and CashSettlement. Cash-account, balance and date-period relationships are preserved without deriving payment directions.

title: Operational transactions, system and account model
meaning: Standing orders have separate credit-account and debit-account associations. CashStandingOrder specializes StandingOrder and links cash-management services. Liquidity limits connect service and exchange context. System information, identification, events, availability and status are separate components. SystemMemberRole and TransactionAdministrator specialize SystemPartyRole; their account, balance, system-status and clearing-system associations are retained. CashAccount and Account remain separate visible nodes; the source view does not draw a generalization between them.

title: Bank-to-customer account conceptual model
meaning: AccountOwnerRole and AccountServicerRole specialize AccountPartyRole. This preserves their conceptual role distinction without equating either with an institution. Account has status, identification, balance, entries and a parent/sub-account self-association. Cash and securities accounts specialize Account; CashEntry specializes Entry. Interest, interest tax, payment and payment identification remain explicitly connected.

title: Bank-to-customer accounts, balances and entries
meaning: Account, Entry and Balance each have cash and securities specializations. AccountLink connects SecuritiesAccount and CashAccount. Account types and bank transactions link to GenericIdentification; Entry connects BankTransaction through the printed BankTransactionCode end label. The general Account–Balance and specific CashAccount–CashBalance lines are both retained. Most source boxes omit stereotypes; only the printed BusinessComponent stereotypes are reconstructed.
